finding.claim: The /logo handler validates the logo parameter only with strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") and then fetches the unmodified raw string with http.Get, letting an attacker reach arbitrary hosts (e.g. cloud metadata or internal services) by placing 'example.io' anywhere in the URL, and reads the response back via io.Copy.
finding.source: r.FormValue("logo") at main.go:31 (attacker-controlled query or form body)
finding.sink: http.Get(raw) at main.go:36, response body copied to the client at main.go:38

trace.note: strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") is the only check; matches anywhere in the string (userinfo, path, query, fragment)
http.Get(raw) fetches the original unparsed string; default client follows redirects; no scheme, host, or IP restriction
io.Copy(w, resp.Body) returns the fetched body to the attacker, making the SSRF readable

finding.guards_checked: Only strings.Contains at line 32. No url.Parse, no scheme check (http/https), no Hostname() allowlist match, no resolved-IP check, no redirect restriction, no DNS-rebinding protection. Bypass examples verified by reading Go net/url semantics (not executed): http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/...?example.io (query); http://example.io@127.0.0.1:8081/cdn?u=... (userinfo, real host 127.0.0.1); http://attacker.example/example.io (path); http://example.io.attacker.example/ (attacker-owned domain).

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check in the logo handler is strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") at main.go:32, which is a substring match and does not close the finding. The trusted-hostname map at main.go:10 and its check at main.go:20 belong to the separate cdn handler and are not applied to /logo. No url.Parse, scheme check, hostname membership, or IP restriction exists on the logo path, and the default http.Get client follows redirects.
verdict.reason: The source is r.FormValue("logo") at main.go:31, which an unauthenticated remote client fully controls. The only check, strings.Contains at main.go:32, is a substring match. The unparsed string is then passed to http.Get at main.go:36, and the response is returned to the client via io.Copy at main.go:38, so the SSRF is readable. Every trace line matches the file as described.
